messages:
maria: Heads-up — support escalated a customer report and a pen test note that look related. They see intermittent 403s when replaying saved requests and the pen tester claims they could infer KMS-encrypted object access from our audit logs. Can we triage?
ashok: which customer / org id? any PII in the logs?
maria: Org: acme-ml (ticket #4572). No PII shared in the sample — just presign and GetObject patterns, timestamps, and a repeated SES-like auth header. Pen report attached to the ticket: short write-up + sampling of audit lines.
penbot: automated-pen-report: finding KMS-AUD-002: narrow timing + presign signature pattern may allow inference of key usage frequency. Severity: medium (awaiting human review).
julia: sharing repro steps I ran quickly: 1) pull audit slice for s3_presign events 2) group by key ARN 3) look for repeating latencies that map to requester IPs. I can reproduce a pattern but not key material.
ben-sre: can you paste the exact query you used for the audit logs? need to replicate locally.
julia: sure — query snippet: ```json
{"query":"resource:presign AND event:CreatePresignedUrl AND time>\"2026-03-01\""}
```
maria: Support also noticed a billing spike at same time window — a bot replaying presign + replays of signed URLs. Could be heavy retry traffic. Not sure if auth fallback caused 403s.
ashok: two tracks: 1) security: verify whether audit logs expose anything beyond metadata (no key material) and confirm severity; 2) infra: reproduce 403s + test if retries/billing correlate with a misconfigured CDN/auth proxy.
julia: For security: I reviewed the audit retention config — we keep full event metadata for 90 days and redact request bodies; key ARNs are stored. KMS HSM key material is never logged.
ben-sre: I'll spin up a minimal replay of the pattern against staging and toggle the auth proxy rules. Will grab traces and Cloudtrail correlation.
maria: can someone confirm whether KMS alias listing is available to non-admins? pen report hinted at alias enumeration from logs. That would bump severity.
ashok: alias listing requires kms:ListAliases — not allowed to regular service accounts. The only risk is if audit log lines leak alias ARNs; but those are resource ids, not secret. We should confirm which fields were included in the sample.
ashok: @ops-bot could you attach the exact log snippets (redacted) that support emailed to us?
ops-bot: uploaded 3 redacted log snippets to ticket #4572 — link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/4572 (logs redact IPs and bodies) :paperclip:
maria: Thanks. Next actions: julia to run a focused audit-query to validate whether alias ARNs appear in non-admin views; ben-sre to reproduce 403/retry load in staging and capture traces; ashok to propose severity (tentative: medium) and coordinate a retest with the pen team once both evidence chains are ready.
julia: noted — I'll share query + output by EOD.
ben-sre: will post staging traces in thread when done, including a short reproduction script.
ashok: if staging confirms pattern we should mitigate with short-term log field redaction and throttle rules on presign endpoints. I'll draft mitigation checklist.
maria: one more ask from legal: retention window vs. regulator RFP — please confirm no unredacted PII in logs.
julia: confirmed — no PII in the samples.
penbot: automated-pen-report: follow-up required. Please update severity in the report after human triage.
maria: ok team — let's sync in 2 hours for a quick status update. :thumbsup:
